articles.title: Does the word ‘Dumbass’ flash up when your husband calls your phone? | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: From ‘Sharon London Sex’ to ‘Trashy Anne’, the names saved in our phones are tiny records of how relationships began. Why erase the evidence? At first glance, it’s such a simple, reasonable ask.
body: Personally, I’ve never got over noticing – on their reality show rather than while lunching – that Kim Kardashian has her mother saved as Kris Jenner instead of, say, Mom. It felt like an extremely revealing detail from the queen of the genre.

The Threads debate raised an interesting question, though: should your contact list be amended and updated, or preserved as a historical artefact? Perhaps the poster is underestimating the warm glow to the heart and soul he subconsciously receives whenever his wife’s name pops up and he’s transported back to the beginning of their unlikely love story. Living app-ily ever after is rare, after all.

Other replies echoed the notion that contacts provoke memories. “I’m coming up on the 10th anniversary of ‘Trashy Anne’ … who I got to know volunteering as bin collectors at a local festival,” said one. Another confided: “My best friend and I met through a mutual friend almost 15 years ago. I’m still ‘Ayannah (Gabby’s friend)’.” The comfort we get from a reminder of these origin stories may be more important than it seems.
points: From ‘Sharon London Sex’ to ‘Trashy Anne’, the names saved in our phones are tiny records of how relationships began.
At first glance, it’s such a simple, reasonable ask.

articles.title: John Cooper Clarke looks back: ‘Getting older sucks – it’s marginally better than being dead’
articles.summary: The punk poet on his heroin years, dressing like Ronnie Wood, and achieving his boyhood ambition. Born in Salford in 1949, John Cooper Clarke is a poet and author. He cut his teeth in the clubs of Manchester before signing to Epic Records in 1978.
body: This is me dressed up as a cowboy with a hat and six-shooter. Not the full schmear with the chaps and all the rest, but the best I could do. I was crazy about westerns. Still am, actually. My uncle Dennis was the only camera-owning relative at the time, so he would have taken the photo in our apartment above a chemist’s shop in Salford, located on a busy traffic intersection.

My childhood is an ever-fading mystery to me, but somewhere around this time I know I got diagnosed with tuberculosis. Something serious like that takes you out of the world, but once I stopped coughing up arterial blood and scar tissue it wasn’t a problem. I stopped going to school, which was great, and not before I’d learned the rudiments of literacy. Really it happened at an opportune moment in that all that I had any energy to do was read.

articles.title: Are my gen X peers the influencers the world has been waiting for? | Emma Beddington
articles.summary: Their careers are peaking, they’re rich in money and time – and young people think they’re cool. But maybe it’s not as simple as that. ‘Stop sleeping on gen X.” I heard this on TikTok recently.
body: Aged between 46 and 61, gen Xers with proper jobs are peaking, career-wise (although it’s a different story for those out of work, as a report last month on the struggles of over-50s jobseekers made plain). We’re more likely to own homes than the following generations; we’re emerging from the trenches of childrearing and, the argument goes, ready to indulge in some me-time. “If gen X were a country, it would be the world’s second-largest consumer market,” the World Economic Forum reported last year, with gen X women in particular influencing 70% to 80% of all consumer spending.

That makes us great customers – witness the tidal wave of menopause-washed wellness guff (Which? reported last month that many pricey supplements were no better than a cheap multivitamin ) and beauty brands for people suddenly horrified by their necks. But does it give us content-creating clout? We’re supposed to be (or at least meme lore presents us as ) the forgotten generation, low-key, countercultural slackers on the sidelines in the grudge match between millennials and boomers; aspiration and self-promotion aren’t really part of our brand.
points: Their careers are peaking, they’re rich in money and time – and young people think they’re cool.
But maybe it’s not as simple as that. ‘Stop sleeping on gen X.

articles.title: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind
articles.summary: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption. There’s a common fear among people who work in Silicon Valley: snag one of the fast-growing, high-paying jobs in artificial intelligence, or get trapped in the “permanent underclass”, a…
body: The phrase usually describes a future in which AI automates human jobs. But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

“A lot of people say: ‘Oh, AI is lowering barriers, it’s equalizing the playing field for women,’” said Urvashi Batra, co-founder and CEO of Prioriwise, an AI platform for IT service providers. “I actually think it’s the opposite.”

Batra said people take her less seriously as the founder of an AI company than her male co-founder. When pitching investors, she and her co-founder have learned that they are more likely to get an investment if he does the pitching.

Women made up only about a quarter of new hires in AI roles in the last year, compared to 50% of new hires in non-AI roles, according to a recent report from LinkedIn. In executive roles, that number drops to just 13%. At the same time, LinkedIn’s research shows that women are more likely to work in roles with high exposure to AI disruption, like customer service, meaning they are also at higher risk for job loss due to AI.
points: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption.
But for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

articles.title: Gigi Hadid Channels Classic French Girl Style in Paris
articles.summary: Fresh off walking the Miu Miu runway, the model emerged looking like a true Parisian—oui, oui, Gigi!
body: Gigi Hadid has been busy making her Fashion Month rounds. In New York, the model first walked for Tommy Hilfiger at the Plaza Hotel. In Milan, she then continued the fun at the Vogue World: Milano show ( wearing Valentino Couture, no less). And now, today in Paris, she marked her third fab show of the season—sauntering down the Miu Miu spring 2027 catwalk in a sports bra and bejeweled skirt. However, it was her post-show outfit that caught our eye.

Call it her off-duty look, but Hadid emerged after the show wearing a classic French girl outfit. The white button-up shirt, straight-leg jeans, and Mary Jane flats ticked all the boxes of true Parisian style. There was a sense of timelessness to the ensemble, not to mention it felt so effortlessly chic. Her accessories, like the brown leather belt and bag to match, were discrete yet polished. And having the shirt unbuttoned just enough to see a peak of her bra top underneath? Chef’s kiss—a perfect nod to her runway look she wore only moments prior.
points: Fresh off walking the Miu Miu runway, the model emerged looking like a true Parisian—oui, oui, Gigi!

articles.title: On ‘SNL,’ Taylor Swift and Dakota Johnson Prove Bestie Style Doesn’t Have to Mean Matchy-Matchy
articles.summary: Taylor Swift joined her “Patient Zero” costar during her “Saturday Night Live” monologue, with the friends trading their co-ords for two very different takes on the statement mini.
body: Just a week after Dakota Johnson and Taylor Swift indulged in some bestie dressing in the latter’s “Patient Zero” music video, the pair are making the case for sartorial independence.

On Saturday night, Swift made a surprise appearance during Johnson’s Saturday Night Live opening monologue, where the actor was hosting for the third time. Johnson, reflecting on the romantic upheavals since her last stint on the Studio 8H stage, credited her friends with seeing her through. Cue Swift, whom Johnson introduced as her “literal therapist.” Swift quickly clarified the arrangement: Johnson simply turns up at her house once a week and eventually has to be driven home by her security.

The cameo also doubled as a fashionable reunion. Johnson, styled by Kate Young, went full 2013 bombshell in a scarlet latex Versace mini dress, paired with Giuseppe Zanotti Intriigo 90 mules. As though the high-shine red number needed any additional wattage, she added Roberto Coin diamonds and rubies, including the $124,000 Wide Cobra Collar and a Cento Circle of Life ring.
points: Taylor Swift joined her “Patient Zero” costar during her “Saturday Night Live” monologue, with the friends trading their co-ords for two very different takes on the statement mini.

articles.summary: For her Paris Fashion Week runway debut, 20-year-old Lily Brant took a little advice from Stephanie Seymour and revisited her lifelong connection to Alaïa.
body: Lily Brant began her trip to Paris as a lot of young women do: visiting favorite restaurants, wandering pretty side streets, and finding a little bistro where she might while away an hour with a coffee and a book—Patti Smith’s Just Kids for pleasure and Pride and Prejudice for college. (“I like reading Pride and Prejudice in an accent,” she tells Vogue. “That helps me!”) There was an Elizabeth Peyton exhibition at the Louvre, dinner with her parents and brother at their beloved Le Stresa, and an evening spent taking in the Eiffel Tower from a rooftop. There was also, of course, the small matter of making her runway debut at Alaïa.

articles.title: Olivia Colman Is Now a Miu Miu Runway Model
articles.summary: The Oscar winner popped up on the runway in Paris as part of a line-up that also included her “Pride & Prejudice” co-star, Emma Corrin.
body: The unexpected catwalk cameo is pretty much fashion week tradition at this point—as par for the course in Paris as street style photographers, traffic, and twice-baked potatoes at Caviar Kaspia. Designers have put OG supers, rappers, actors, and even fashion critics on the runway in recent seasons, and a liberal sprinkling of nepo babies is now a given. But arguably no one does stunt casting better than Mrs. Prada (it was Miuccia who so memorably assembled a team of Hollywood “villains” that included Gary Oldman and Willem Dafoe for the fall 2012 Prada show ), and she pulled off another surprise in Paris today, where Olivia Colman just walked the Miu Miu runway.

Happily for guests at today’s show, the 52-year-old ( who revealed a new look earlier in the week while promoting her film Wicker ) was persuaded to put all that aside to join Mrs P’s characteristically eclectic model line-up. Also spotted on the runway? Hamnet star Noah Jupe, Jamie Bell, Louisa Jacobson (daughter of Meryl Streep), and Ella Bleu Travolta (daughter of John)—like we said, it’s a given.
